newsitem.title: MEXICO: China sugar policy based on self-sufficiency - ISO.
newsitem.headline: China sugar policy based on self-sufficiency - ISO.

text.p: China's sugar policy, although not explicitly stated, is based on self-sufficiency, with imports covering only output shortfalls, the head of the International Sugar Organisation's economic and statistics division said here Wednesday.

Tony Hannah told the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference that despite the world sugar markets' view that Chinese consumption will take off in the future, the Beijing government "has other ideas."
Alongside the import-only-when-shortfall stance taken by the Chinese is also the substitution of saccharin for sugar if consumption rises or if import prices are too high, Hannah said .

"Recent development provide supporting evidence. In 1992, Chinese production surged to 8.86 million tonnes from 6.9 million tonnes in 1991. But the dramatically increased availability was not assigned to consumption, rather China became a net exporter of 705,000 tonnes in 1992 and 1.55 million tonnes in 1993," Hannah said.

"Sharp falls in production in 1994 and 1995 returned China to net importer status, but with sugar consumption remaining sluggish through the 1990s, there is no sign of a change in the implicit guiding policy," he said, adding China's per capita consumption is around 6 kg.
"The figures vary enormously from year to year and we do not see that changing in the long term. There are large variations year to year depending on production," he added.
Hannah said there was no indication of a change in the policy of self-sufficiency.

"Therefore, no change is anticipated in China's long-term average imports of 1.5 million tonnes....Consumption of soft drinks by the urban middle class will continue to grow, but the substitution of saccharine according to the availablity of domestically produced sugar will also continue," he added.
